en: Udāna 8.9 Paṭhamadabbasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Then the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
As he was sitting there, the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta said this to the Blessed One:
“Now is the time for my final Nibbāna, O Sugata.
“Do as you think it is now time for, Dabba,” [the Blessed One replied].
Then the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, and circumambulated him.
Having risen up into the air and seated himself cross-legged in the sky, in the firmament, he entered the fire-element, emerged from it,
and attained final nibbāna. Then,
as the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta had risen up into the air and was seated cross-legged in the sky, in the firmament—
Having sat down, entered the fire-element, and emerged, when his body had attained final Nibbāna and was burning and being consumed,
neither ash nor soot could be discerned.
Just as, for example, when ghee or oil is burning and being consumed, neither ash nor soot can be discerned.
In this very way, when the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta had ascended into the air, sat cross-legged in the sky in mid-air,
entered the fire-element, emerged from it, and attained final nibbāna, as his body was burning and being consumed,
neither ash nor soot was perceived.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“The body has broken up, perception has ceased;
all feelings have grown cold.”
“Formations have been stilled;
consciousness has come to its end. Thus ends the ninth [sutta].
